questions.question: The median of the observations 76, 83, 30, 11, 81, 52, 18, 34, 84, 35 and 27 is:

questions.question: The mode and median of a data set is 28.4 and 88, respectively. What is the mean of the data set? (Use empirical formula.)

According to the empirical formula: Mean = (3 × Median − Mode) ÷ 2

⇒ Mean = (264 − 28.4) ÷ 2

⇒ Mean = 235.6 ÷ 2 = 117.8

If the mode of the following data is 140, then what is the value of x?

 
 

 Class

 135-140
 140-145
 145-150
 
 
 
 

 Frequency
 30
 30
 33
 x
 31
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Classes: 125–130(30), 130–135(30), 135–140(33), 140–145(x), 145–150(31)

**Formula used:**

 {Mode} = l + (f₁ - f₀)/(2f₁ - f₀ - f₂)times h

Where: Modal class = one containing the mode (140–145):

l = 140, f₁ = x, f₀ = 33, f₂ = 31, h = 5

**Calculations:**

Mode = 140, so

140 = 140 + (x-33)/(2x -33 -31)×5

⇒ (x-33)/(2x -64)×5 = 0

⇒ 5x - 165 = 0

⇒ x = 165/5

⇒ x = 33

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Marks in statistics of 12 students are x, 28, 35, 56, 78, 63, 65, 81, 79, 83, 80, y, where x and y are the lowest and highest marks, respectively. If the range and average of the marks are 70 and 64, respectively, then the ordered pair (x, y) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marks of 12 students: x, 28, 35, 56, 78, 63, 65, 81, 79, 83, 80, y

Range = 70

Average = 64

x = Lowest mark, y = Highest mark

**Formula used:**

Range = y - x

Average = dfrac{{Sum of all marks}}{{Total number of students}}

**Calculation:**

Range = y - x

⇒ 70 = y - x

⇒ y = x + 70

Average = dfrac{{Sum of all marks}}{12}

⇒ 64 = dfrac{x + 28 + 35 + 56 + 78 + 63 + 65 + 81 + 79 + 83 + 80 + y}{12}

⇒ 64 × 12 = x + 28 + 35 + 56 + 78 + 63 + 65 + 81 + 79 + 83 + 80 + y

⇒ 768 = x + y + (28 + 35 + 56 + 78 + 63 + 65 + 81 + 79 + 83 + 80)

⇒ 768 = x + y + 648

⇒ x + y = 768 - 648

⇒ x + y = 120

Solving for x and y:

From y = x + 70 and x + y = 120, substitute y = x + 70:

⇒ x + (x + 70) = 120

⇒ 2x + 70 = 120

⇒ 2x = 120 - 70

⇒ 2x = 50

⇒ x = 25

Substitute x = 25 in y = x + 70:

⇒ y = 25 + 70

⇒ y = 95

**∴ The ordered pair (x, y) = (25, 95).**

**The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: The mode and median of a dataset is 52.7 and 65, respectively. What is the mean of the dataset? (Use empirical formula, and round off your answer to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mode = 52.7

Median = 65

**Formula Used:**

Empirical formula: Mean - Mode = 3 × (Mean - Median)

**Calculations:**

Mean - 52.7 = 3 × (Mean - 65)

⇒ Mean - 52.7 = 3 × Mean - 3 × 65

⇒ Mean - 52.7 = 3 × Mean - 195

⇒ 195 - 52.7 = 3 × Mean - Mean

⇒ 142.3 = 2 × Mean

⇒ Mean = 142.3 / 2

⇒ Mean = 71.15

⇒ Mean ≈ 71.2

The **mean** of the dataset is **71.2**.

questions.solution:

Mode approx 3 Median - 2 Mean

**Calculations:**

Rearrange the empirical formula to find the Mean:

2 Mean approx 3 Median - Mode

Mean approx ((3 times Median) - Mode)/(2)

Substitute the given values:

Mean approx ((3 times 32) - 89.7)/(2) 

⇒ Mean approx (96 - 89.7)/(2)

⇒ Mean approx (6.3)/(2)

questions.question: Following are the ages (in years) of 6 people in a group: 25, 30, 35, 40, 45 and 50. What is the standard deviation of their ages (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ages of the group: 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50

n = 6

**Formula used:**

Standard Deviation (σ) = sqrt{dfrac{sum(x_i - mu)²}{n}}

Where:

n = number of data points

mu = mean of the data points

(x_i) = each data point

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Calculate the mean:

mu = dfrac{{Sum of ages}}{n}

⇒ mu = dfrac{25+30+35+40+45+50}{6}

⇒ mu = dfrac{225}{6} = 37.5

Step 2: Calculate the squared differences from the mean:

(x_i - mu)² for each data point:

For 25: (25 - 37.5)² = (-12.5)² = 156.25

For 30: (30 - 37.5)² = (-7.5)² = 56.25

For 35: (35 - 37.5)² = (-2.5)² = 6.25

For 40: (40 - 37.5)² = (2.5)² = 6.25

For 45: (45 - 37.5)² = (7.5)² = 56.25

For 50: (50 - 37.5)² = (12.5)² = 156.25

Step 3: Calculate the variance:

Variance = dfrac{{Sum of squared differences}}{n}

⇒ Variance = dfrac{156.25+56.25+6.25+6.25+56.25+156.25}{6}

⇒ Variance = dfrac{437.5}{6} = 72.92

Step 4: Calculate the standard deviation:

σ = sqrt{72.92}

⇒ σ = 8.54

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 12.6, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mode exceeds Mean by 12.6

**Formula used:**

Empirical formula: Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

**Calculation:**

Let Mean = M and Median = Md

Mode = 3(Md) - 2(M)

Given, Mode - Mean = 12.6

⇒ [3(Md) - 2(M)] - M = 12.6

⇒ 3(Md) - 3(M) = 12.6

⇒ Md - M = 12.6 ÷ 3

⇒ Md - M = 4.2

Mode exceeds Median by:

Mode - Median = [3(Md) - 2(M)] - Md

⇒ 2(Md) - 2(M)

⇒ 2(Md - M)

⇒ 2 × 4.2 = 8.4

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: If the mode of a data set exceeds its mean by 17.7, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:

Mode exceeds mean by 17.7

**Formula used:**

Empirical formula: Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

**Calculation:**

Using the formula, Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

Let Mean = x

Mode = x + 17.7

⇒ x + 17.7 = 3(Median) - 2(x)

⇒ x + 17.7 + 2x = 3(Median)

⇒ 3x + 17.7 = 3(Median)

⇒ Median = x + 5.9

Mode exceeds Median:

⇒ Mode - Median = (x + 17.7) - (x + 5.9)

⇒ = 17.7 - 5.9

⇒ = 11.8

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: The mean and standard deviation of 100 terms are 50 and 3, respectively. The sum of squares of the 100 terms is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mean (μ) = 50

Standard Deviation (σ) = 3

Total terms (n) = 100

**Formula used:**

Sum of squares of terms = n × (μ² + σ²)

**Calculation:**

Sum of squares of terms = 100 × (50² + 3²)

⇒ Sum of squares of terms = 100 × (2500 + 9)

⇒ Sum of squares of terms = 100 × 2509

⇒ Sum of squares of terms = 2,50,900

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of terms (n) = 100

Mean (xbₐᵣ) = 50

Standard Deviation (σ) = 3

**Formula used:**

Standard Deviation (σ) = √((Σx² ÷ n) − (xbₐᵣ)²)

Where, Σx² = sum of squares of terms

**Calculations:**

We have σ² = (Σx² ÷ n) − (xbₐᵣ)²

⇒ Σx² = n(σ² + (xbₐᵣ)²)

⇒ Σx² = 100(3² + 50²)

⇒ Σx² = 100(9 + 2500)

⇒ Σx² = 100 × 2509

⇒ Σx² = 250900

**∴ The sum of squares of the 100 terms is 250900.**

questions.question:
If the mode of the following data is 165, then what is the value of x?

 
 

 Class
 150-155
 155-160
 160-165
 165-170
 170-175
 
 
 
 

 Frequency
 23
 25
 37
 x
 28
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Class:

150-155, 155-160, 160-165, 165-170, 170-175

Frequency:

23, 25, 37, x, 28

Mode = 165

**Formula used:**

Mode = L + (f₁ - f₀) / (2f₁ - f₀ - f₂) × h

Where:

L = lower boundary of modal class

f₁ = frequency of modal class

f₀ = frequency of class preceding modal class

f₂ = frequency of class succeeding modal class

h = class width

**Calculation:**

Mode = 165

L = 160

f₁ = 37

f₀ = 25

f₂ = x

h = 5

165 = 160 + (37 - 25) / (2 × 37 - 25 - x) × 5

⇒ 165 = 160 + 12 / (74 - 25 - x) × 5

⇒ 165 - 160 = (12 × 5) / (49 - x)

⇒ 5 = 60 / (49 - x)

⇒ 5 × (49 - x) = 60

⇒ 245 - 5x = 60

⇒ 185 = 5x

⇒ x = 37

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**
